blocks.text: Built an AI-assisted dental billing audit system that reviews Explanation of Benefits (EOB) documents — the summaries insurers send after processing a dental claim — looks up relevant insurance policy rules, and flags possible billing discrepancies with supporting evidence for human review. Reduced per-claim review time from 15 minutes to under 1 minute while improving consistency and explainability.
Problem

Dental EOBs are difficult to interpret because payment decisions depend on plan-specific policies, fee schedules, coverage limits, exclusions, deductibles, annual maximums, and procedure-level reimbursement rules. Manual review is slow, inconsistent, and hard to scale.
Patients often cannot tell whether a claim was paid correctly without understanding their specific plan rules.
Billing teams reviewing high volumes frequently miss discrepancies under time pressure.
Relevant policy language is buried in lengthy plan documents — not available at the point of review.
No scalable system existed to compare claim outcomes against the actual plan rules that should apply.
Users & Stakeholders

items.title: Patients
items.description: Trying to understand whether they were billed or reimbursed correctly by their dental plan.

items.title: Dental Billing Teams
items.description: Reviewing reimbursement accuracy across high claim volumes with limited time per claim.

items.title: Support Staff
items.description: Explaining claim outcomes and resolving disputes with payers.

items.title: Operators
items.description: Triaging flagged cases and managing escalation for complex or ambiguous claims.

blocks.text: Product Goal
Reduce the time it takes to review a dental EOB while making findings more consistent and easier to verify — without pretending every claim can be safely automated.
How It Works

This is not just a Large Language Model (LLM) reviewing a PDF. It is a hybrid AI workflow with four distinct layers: document extraction, policy lookup, rules-based checks, and AI reasoning. Each layer handles a different part of the problem. Together they produce findings that are consistent, explainable, and grounded in actual source policy documents.

items.title: EOB Extraction
items.description: Uses Optical Character Recognition (OCR) — software that reads text from scanned documents — to extract key claim fields: procedure codes, billed amount, allowed amount, paid amount, patient responsibility, deductible applied, and plan details.

items.title: Policy Knowledge Base
items.description: Dental insurance policies, fee schedules, coverage rules, exclusions, reimbursement guidelines, and Current Dental Terminology (CDT) procedure code definitions are imported into a searchable knowledge base.

items.title: Policy Lookup (RAG)
items.description: For each claim, the system retrieves the most relevant policy sections before generating a finding. This approach — called Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — keeps AI reasoning grounded in source documents instead of general knowledge.

items.title: Rules-Based Checks
items.description: Automated checks for known billing problems: duplicate procedure codes, unbundled services, frequency limit violations, and missing prior authorizations.

items.title: AI Reasoning
items.description: The LLM interprets complex or ambiguous policy language that rules-based checks cannot handle — such as determining whether a specific exclusion applies to a given procedure.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop Review
items.description: Low-confidence or high-risk findings are flagged for human review instead of being shown as conclusions. The system supports reviewers — it does not replace them.

blocks.text: Audit Workflow
Why RAG?

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) means the system searches a knowledge base before generating an answer — rather than relying only on what the AI was trained to know. For BillHero, I imported dental insurance policies, fee schedules, reimbursement rules, exclusions, and plan-specific documents into a searchable knowledge base. For each claim, the system retrieves the most relevant policy sections before generating a discrepancy finding. This keeps outputs grounded in actual source documents and reduces hallucinations — unsupported claims the AI might otherwise produce.

blocks.text: Evaluation & Quality Controls
I built an evaluation set — a test group of labeled EOBs with expected discrepancy findings — to measure how well the system worked before trusting its output.
Extraction accuracy: did the system correctly read claim fields like procedure codes, amounts, and deductibles from the EOB?
Retrieval quality: did the policy lookup surface the right sections for the specific claim and procedure being reviewed?
Source grounding: did each finding trace back to real policy language rather than general AI knowledge?
Hallucination checks: did the system avoid making unsupported claims — findings that could not be verified in the source policy documents?
Precision: when the system flagged a discrepancy, was it actually a real problem worth reviewing?
Recall: was the system catching the important discrepancies, or missing cases it should have flagged?
Human-in-the-loop routing: did ambiguous and high-risk cases get escalated to a human reviewer instead of being automatically resolved?
Key Product Decisions

blocks.decision: Rules + AI instead of AI alone
blocks.tradeoff: Using only an LLM would miss clear billing violations that can be caught with simple rules — and would be harder to audit and explain.
blocks.outcome: Rules-based checks handle unambiguous billing problems. The LLM handles cases where policy language is complex or context-dependent.

blocks.tradeoff: Dental plan rules vary by payer and change over time. Retraining a model every time a policy updates is not practical.
blocks.outcome: RAG lets the system search the most current policy documents at query time — no retraining needed when rules change.

blocks.tradeoff: Fully automated claim adjudication would be faster but difficult to verify and hard to trust in a billing context.
blocks.outcome: Every finding includes the policy section it came from and a confidence score. Outputs are designed for human review, not to replace it.

blocks.tradeoff: Showing every finding regardless of confidence would flood reviewers with noise and erode trust in the system.
blocks.outcome: High-confidence findings are prioritized. Low-confidence cases are routed to a human reviewer rather than surfaced as conclusions.

blocks.text: Before vs. After

blocks.title: Manual Review vs. AI-Assisted Audit
before: Discrepancies easy to miss under time pressure
No policy evidence surfaced at review
after: Policy context retrieved and cited automatically
Consistent structured findings across all claims
Human review focused on ambiguous cases only

blocks.text: Results & Impact
Reduced per-claim review time from 15 minutes to under 1 minute.
Surfaced 1–3 likely discrepancies per reviewed EOB on average.
Every finding includes a policy citation and confidence score — making it easy to verify or escalate.
Built and validated against a simulated evaluation set to confirm extraction accuracy, retrieval quality, and source grounding.
Demonstrated how RAG-grounded AI can reduce manual review time while keeping a human in the loop for complex and ambiguous cases.
What I Would Do Next
Build payer-specific policy libraries covering major dental insurance carriers.
Expand CDT procedure code coverage and reimbursement rule depth.
Add a batch review mode for billing teams processing high claim volumes.
Track precision and recall across larger labeled evaluation sets.
Add reviewer feedback loops to improve retrieval quality and discrepancy classification over time.
